record.title: Four-color conjecture for ISK4-free graphs
record.statement: A graph is **ISK4-free** if it has no induced subdivision of $K_4$. **ISK4-free four-color conjecture.** Every ISK4-free graph is 4-colorable. The preceding theorem gives a constant bound on the chromatic number of ISK4-free graphs, and the source notes that no example with chromatic number at least $5$ is known.
record.source_name: Benjamin Lévêque, Frédéric Maffray and Nicolas Trotignon, “On graphs with no induced subdivision of K_4”, arXiv:1309.1926 (2013).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1309.1926

Status: **refuted** according to the source (as of September 2013). “This conjectured was disproved by Pawlick et al.\ .”

record.title: Hefetz's acyclic-set conjecture for planar digraphs
record.statement:
Let $D$ be a simple planar digraph on $n$ vertices. An **acyclic set** is a vertex set inducing no directed cycle in $D$. **Hefetz's conjecture.** Every simple $n$-vertex planar digraph has an acyclic set of size at least

$$
\tfrac{3n}{5}.
$$

The conjecture is cited as supporting evidence for the broader 2-colorability problem, but no resolution is given in the source.
record.source_name: Ararat Harutyunyan and Bojan Mohar, “Planar digraphs of digirth five are 2-colorable”, arXiv:1401.2213 (2014).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.2213

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of January 2014).

record.title: The detachable-pair classification conjecture for 3-connected matroids
record.statement:
Let $M$ be a $3$-connected matroid with $|E(M)| \ge 13$.

**Detachable-pair classification conjecture.** Either $M$ has a detachable pair; $M$ is a spike; $M \cong M(K_{3,k})$ or $M \cong M^*(K_{3,k})$ for some $k \ge 5$; $M$ is the cycle matroid of a wheel or a whirl; $M$ can be constructed by attaching wheels to a spike with tip and cotip; or $M$ or $M^*$ can be constructed by attaching wheels with common spokes $s$ and $t$, and then deleting $s$.

This conjecture classifies the exceptional $3$-connected matroids with no detachable pair once the ground set has at least thirteen elements. The preceding discussion identifies several families with no detachable pairs, including spikes, wheel and whirl matroids, and matroids obtained by attaching wheels; the classification remains unproved in the supplied text.
record.source_name: Nick Brettell, Geoff Whittle and Alan Williams, “N-detachable pairs in 3-connected matroids III: the theorem”, arXiv:1804.06588 (2021).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1804.06588

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of April 2018).

record.title: A colorability bound for the hat chromatic number
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a graph. Write $\operatorname{col}(G)$ for its coloring number and let $\mu(G)$ denote its hat chromatic number. **Coloring-number conjecture.** There is a function $F$ such that every graph $G$ satisfies

$$
\mu(G)\leqslant F(\operatorname{col}(G)).
$$

The theorem on $k$-stars implies that any such function must satisfy $F(k)\geqslant 2^{k-1}$.
record.source_name: Bartłomiej Bosek, Andrzej Dudek, Michał Farnik, Jarosław Grytczuk and Przemysław Mazur, “Hat chromatic number of graphs”, arXiv:1905.04108 (2019).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1905.04108

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of May 2019).

record.title: Wang's minimum semi-degree conjecture for disjoint directed cycles
record.statement:
Let $D$ be a digraph of order $n$, where $k\geq 1$ is an integer and $n\geq 3k$.

**Wang's conjecture.** If $\delta^0(D)\geq (9k-3)/4$, then $D$ contains $k$ vertex-disjoint directed cycles, each of order at least $3$.

The source presents this as one of Wang's conjectures on disjoint cycles in digraphs. Its status is not established in the source.
record.source_name: Yun Wang and Jin Yan, “On directed version of the Sauer-Spender Theorem”, arXiv:2001.11703 (2020).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2001.11703

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of January 2020).

record.title: Hippchen's conjecture for 5-connected graphs
record.statement: Let $G$ be a 5-connected graph. **5-connected Hippchen conjecture.** Every pair of longest paths intersect each other in at least five vertices. The paper proves the analogous statement for 4-connected graphs and proposes this 5-connected extension; it remains open in the source.
record.source_name: Juan Gutiérrez, “On the intersection of two longest paths in k-connected graphs”, arXiv:2008.02163 (2020).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2008.02163

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of August 2020).

record.title: Exact maximization conjecture for minimal codewords in binary linear codes of codimension three
record.statement:
Let $C$ be a binary linear $[k+3,k]_2$ code, and let $M_2(k+3,k)$ denote the maximum possible number of minimal codewords among such codes. For $k\geq 4$, write

$$
\mathbf{a}=\left(a_{000},a_{100},a_{010},a_{001},a_{110},a_{101},a_{011},a_{111}\right),
$$

where the entries count the multiplicities of the corresponding information vectors, and let $M_2(k+3,k)$ be evaluated by the formula of Proposition~. **Exact maximization conjecture.** For $k\geq 4$, the exact value of $M_2(k+3,k)$ is given by that formula with $\mathbf{a}$ equal to

$$
\left\{
\begin{array}{rcl}
(l,l,l,l+1,l+1,l+1,l+1) &:& k=4+7l,\\
(l,l,l,l+1,l+1,l+1,l+2) &:& k=5+7l,\\
(l,l,l,l+1,l+1,l+2,l+2) &:& k=6+7l,\\
(l,l,l,l+1,l+2,l+2,l+2) &:& k=7+7l,\\
(l+1,l,l,l+2,l+2,l+1,l+2) &:& k=8+7l,\\
(l+1,l,l,l+2,l+2,l+2,l+2) &:& k=9+7l,\\
(l+1,l+1,l,l+2,l+2,l+2,l+2) &:& k=10+7l
\end{array}
\right.
$$

if $k\leq 26$; if $k\not\equiv 0\pmod 4$ and $k\geq 27$, then

$$
a_{000}=a_{001}=a_{110}=a_{111}=0,\quad a_{100}=\left\lfloor\frac{k}{4}\right\rfloor,\quad a_{010}=\left\lfloor\frac{k+1}{4}\right\rfloor,\quad a_{101}=\left\lfloor\frac{k+2}{4}\right\rfloor,\quad a_{011}=\left\lfloor\frac{k+3}{4}\right\rfloor;
$$

if $k\equiv 0\pmod 4$ and $k\geq 27$, then

$$
a_{000}=a_{001}=a_{110}=a_{111}=0,\quad a_{100}=\frac{k}{4},\quad a_{010}=\frac{k}{4}-1,\quad a_{101}=\frac{k}{4}+1,\quad a_{011}=\frac{k}{4}.
$$

The conjecture would determine the exact extremal number of minimal codewords for binary codes with codimension three. Its large-$k$ cases are motivated by comparing the leading fourth-degree term, but the exact maximization of the underlying multiplicity formula is described as technically challenging and remains open.
record.source_name: Romar dela Cruz and Sascha Kurz, “On the maximum number of minimal codewords”, arXiv:2010.10762 (2020).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2010.10762

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of October 2020).

record.title: The exact-one-edge transversal conjecture for 5-cycles in triangle-free subcubic graphs
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a triangle-free subcubic graph. **Exact-one-edge 5-cycle conjecture.** There exists a set $E'$ of edges such that every $5$-cycle in $G$ contains exactly one edge from $E'$.

This is posed as a further conjecture about the structure of $5$-cycles in triangle-free subcubic graphs; the supplied text gives no resolution.
record.source_name: Gregory Gutin and Anders Yeo, “Lower Bounds for Maximum Weighted Cut”, arXiv:2104.05536 (2024).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2104.05536

Status: **open** according to the source (as of April 2021).

record.title: Nonexistence of lattice t-PTMCs in the intermediate range
record.statement: Let $\Lambda_n=\mathbb{Z}^n$ and let a lattice $t$-PTMC be a lattice perfect total-multipacking code with parameter $t$. **Nonexistence conjecture.** There is no lattice $t$-PTMC in $\Lambda_n$ for $1<t<n$. The question concerns the existence of lattice perfect total-multipacking codes beyond the known constructions for $t=1$; its resolution is not indicated in the supplied text.
record.source_name: Italo J. Dejter, Luis R. Fuentes and Carlos A. Martinez, “Multilattice graphs and perfect domination”, arXiv:2107.13615 (2022).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2107.13615

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of July 2021).

record.title: Cichacz's conjecture on zero-sum partitions of abelian groups
record.statement:
Let $G$ be an abelian group with at least three involutions, and let $r_1,\dots,r_t\geq 3$ satisfy

$$
r_1+\dots+r_t=|G|-1.
$$

A subset is **zero-sum** if the sum of its elements is zero. **Cichacz's conjecture.** There is a partition

$$
G\setminus\{e\}=Z_1\cup\dots\cup Z_t
$$

where every $Z_i$ is a zero-sum set of size $r_i$. The paper says that its characterization confirms this conjecture.
record.source_name: Alp Müyesser and Alexey Pokrovskiy, “A random Hall-Paige conjecture”, arXiv:2204.09666 (2025).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2204.09666

Status: **solved** according to the source (as of April 2022). “This was confirmed in 2009 by Wilcox, Evans, and Bray with a proof using the classification of finite simple groups.”

record.title: The (2,2) Conjecture for graph edge colorings
record.statement: A $(p,q)$-coloring of a graph $G$ is a decomposition into at most $p$ subgraphs such that, in each subgraph, neighboring vertices can be distinguished by sums using at most $q$ colors. **(2,2) Conjecture.** Every connected graph $G$ of order $n\geq 4$ has a $(2,2)$-coloring.
record.source_name: Igor Grzelec and Mariusz Woźniak, “On decomposing multigraphs into locally irregular submultigraphs”, arXiv:2208.08809 (2022).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2208.08809

Status: **open** according to the source (as of August 2022). “This conjecture remains still open, but there are some important results about the 1-2-3 Conjecture and we refer the reader to the survey .”

record.title: Caterpillar decomposition conjecture for fully leafed Penrose subtrees
record.statement:
Let $T$ be a fully leafed Penrose subtree. A Penrose tree is **saturated** if $n_{1}(T)=\overline{L_{P2}}(n(T))$, where $\overline{L_{P2}}(n)=8n/17+b$ is the unique linear upper bound described in the source, and an **appendix** is a fully leafed induced subtree whose derived subtree contains precisely one leaf of $T$-degree $2$ and at most two cells of $T$-degree $3$. **Caterpillar decomposition conjecture.**

(i) If $T$ is saturated, then $T$ is a caterpillar.

(ii) If $T$ is non-saturated, then there exist a saturated caterpillar $T_1$ and an appendix $T_2$ such that

$$
T=T_1\diamond T_2.
$$

This conjecture proposes that saturated fully leafed Penrose subtrees are exactly caterpillars, while every non-saturated one is obtained by grafting an appendix onto a saturated caterpillar. The source gives this as a formalization of observed structures; no resolution is stated.
record.source_name: Carole Porrier, Alain Goupil and Alexandre Blondin Massé, “The Leaf Function of Penrose P2 Graphs”, arXiv:2312.08262 (2025).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2312.08262

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of December 2023).

record.title: Nonexistence conjecture for perfect codes over non-prime-power alphabets
record.statement:
Let $q \ge 6$ be a non-prime power, and let $Z_q$ denote the alphabet of size $q$.

**Nonexistence conjecture.** Let $q \ge 6$ be a non-prime power. Then, there are no perfect error correcting codes over $Z_q$.

Existing results establish nonexistence for several values of $q$ and error-correction parameters, but the general classification over non-prime-power alphabets remains open.
record.source_name: Pedro-José Cazorla García, “Perfect codes over non-prime power alphabets: an approach based on Diophantine equations”, arXiv:2405.03347 (2024).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2405.03347

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of May 2024).

record.title: The edge-width four conjecture for 5-choosability on the torus
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a graph drawn on the torus. Its **edge-width** is the length of its shortest non-contractible cycle.

**The edge-width four conjecture.** Every graph drawn on the torus with edge-width at least four is $5$-choosable.

This would establish the main 5-choosability conjecture for an important class of toroidal graphs without short non-contractible cycles; it remains open in the source.
record.source_name: Zdeněk Dvořák and Félix Moreno Peñarrubia, “Towards Characterization of 5-List-Colorability of Toroidal Graphs”, arXiv:2407.18800 (2024).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2407.18800

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of July 2024).

record.title: Sheehan's conjecture on 2-factor Hamiltonian regular bipartite graphs
record.statement: Let $G$ be a $2$-factor Hamiltonian $k$-regular bipartite graph, meaning that every $2$-factor of $G$ is a Hamiltonian circuit. **Sheehan's conjecture.** There are no $2$-factor Hamiltonian $k$-regular bipartite graphs for any integer $k\geq 4$. This is the higher-degree exclusion suggested by the classification conjecture above and remains open in the survey.
record.source_name: D. Labbate and F. Romaniello, “An updated survey on 2-Factors of Regular Graphs”, arXiv:2408.04642 (2024).
record.references:
**2 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2017–2024). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:1709.04895](https://arxiv.org/abs/1709.04895).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2408.04642

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of August 2024).

record.title: The bounded multiplicity extension for properly edge-coloured graphs
record.statement: Let $m$ and $k$ be positive integers. **The bounded multiplicity extension.** There exists a graph with chromatic number at least $k$ that has a proper edge-colouring such that each cycle contains no colour between one and $m$ times. This is posed in the concluding remarks as a natural extension of the paper's main result; its status is not resolved in the supplied text.

record.references:

record.title: El Sahili's arc-deletion conjecture for oriented Hamiltonian paths
record.statement:
Let $T$ be a strong tournament of order $n\geq 8$, let $e$ be an arc of $T$, and let $P$ be an oriented path of order $n$. **El Sahili's conjecture.** The tournament $T-e$ contains $P$.

This conjecture proposes that every arc deletion from a strong tournament of order at least eight preserves every oriented Hamiltonian path; the supplied context does not report a proof or disproof.
record.source_name: Mahabba El Sahili and Ayman El Zein, “Oriented Hamiltonian Paths in Tournaments: Stability under Arc Deletion”, arXiv:2512.09332 (2025).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2512.09332

Status: **solved** according to the source (as of December 2025). “This conjecture was proved by Fraisse and Thomassen , and recently a stronger result was proved by Bang-Jensen et al. .”

record.title: Generalized Hamilton-connectedness conjecture for forbidden-star split graphs
record.statement:
Let $r\geq 3$ be an integer. A graph is **split** if its vertex set can be partitioned into a clique and an independent set. It is ${K_{1,r+1},K_{1,r+1}+e}$-free if it contains no induced subgraph isomorphic to either forbidden graph, where $K_{1,r+1}+e$ is obtained from $K_{1,r+1}$ by adding an edge joining two nonadjacent vertices. A graph is **Hamilton-connected** if every two distinct vertices are joined by a Hamiltonian path.

**Generalized Hamilton-connectedness conjecture.** Every $r$-connected ${K_{1,r+1},K_{1,r+1}+e}$-free split graph of order at least $2r+7$ is Hamilton-connected.

The conjecture is motivated by the paper's theorem for $r=3$, namely that every $3$-connected ${K_{1,4},K_{1,4}+e}$-free split graph of order at least $13$ is Hamilton-connected. The general case is posed for further study and is unresolved in the supplied text.
record.source_name: Tao Tian and Fengming Dong, “Every 3-connected \K_1,4,K_1,4+e\-free split graph of order at least 13 is Hamilton-connected”, arXiv:2603.12770 (2026).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.12770

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of March 2026).

record.title: The rational finiteness conjecture for the joint spectral radius
record.statement:
Let $A_1,\ldots,A_m$ be real $n\times n$ matrices with rational entries, and let $\rho(A_1,\ldots,A_m)$ denote their joint spectral radius. Is it always true that there exist a finite length $k\ge 1$ and indices $\sigma_1,\ldots,\sigma_k\in\{1,\ldots,m\}$ such that
\[
\bigl(\rho(A_{\sigma_1}\cdots A_{\sigma_k})\bigr)^{1/k}=\rho(A_1,\ldots,A_m)?
\]
Here the $\rho$ on the left is the ordinary spectral radius, while the $\rho$ on the right is the joint spectral radius.

record.title: Hypergraph cuts above the average: the $m^{2/3}$ excess conjecture
record.statement:
Fix integers $k\ge r\ge 2$ such that $r\ge 3$ or $k\ge 4$. Let $G$ be a $k$-uniform hypergraph with $m$ edges. An $r$-cut of $G$ is a partition of its vertex set into $r$ parts, and its size is the number of edges having at least one vertex in each part. Writing
\[
\alpha_{r,k}=\frac{S(k,r)r!}{r^k},
\]
where $S(k,r)$ is the number of unlabelled partitions of $\{1,\ldots,k\}$ into $r$ nonempty sets, is it true that $G$ has an $r$-cut of size at least
\[
\alpha_{r,k}m+\Omega\!\left(m^{2/3}\right)?
\]
record.source_name: Oberwolfach Reports: 10.4171/OWR/2019/19, page 70
